verdict: Viatris sales were flat at $3.75B, but a $453M tax bill on just $128M of pre-tax profit turned the quarter into a $325M GAAP loss.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: essentially flat vs a year ago

segments.name: Developed Markets
segments.note: Net sales in North America, Europe and other developed markets — down 2% YoY on supply constraints in Europe and added competition.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: Net sales in Greater China — up 14% YoY, the growth engine this quarter.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.note: Net sales in emerging markets — down 7% YoY on supply constraints.

segments.name: JANZ
segments.note: Net sales in Japan, Australia and New Zealand — down 6% YoY.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Revenues other than product net sales, as reported.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Research spending of $232M plus $5M of acquired in-process R&D, as reported.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company — reported SG&A of $951M, net of an $11M litigation settlements credit, in whole $M.

otherDetail: Interest expense $112M plus other expense, net $21M — a $133M net cost in whole-$M figures (the release reports $134M combined).
footerNote: Loss quarter: Viatris made an operating profit, but interest, other expense and an unusually large tax provision produced a GAAP net loss.
oneTimers: Purchase accounting amortization of $614M — a non-cash charge from past acquisitions, mostly in cost of sales — is the biggest reason GAAP gross margin was 38.4% while adjusted gross margin was 58.0%. Adjusted net earnings were $821M ($0.71 per share) versus the GAAP net loss of $325M.

Tax drove the loss: the GAAP tax provision was $453M despite only $128M of pre-tax profit, because losses in some jurisdictions earn minimal tax benefit. The company also recorded $66M of restructuring costs and $66M of other special items in cost of sales in the quarter (both excluded from adjusted results).

takeaways.title: Tax turned profit into loss
takeaways.text: Viatris earned $261M of operating profit, but after $133M of interest and other expense, a $453M tax provision — on only $128M of pre-tax profit — left a $325M GAAP net loss.

takeaways.title: China carried the growth
takeaways.text: Greater China sales rose 14% to $703M and brands like Lipitor ($452M) stayed strong, offsetting a 2% dip in Developed Markets and supply problems in Europe and Emerging Markets.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit rose
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $0.71, up 6%, and adjusted EBITDA rose 4% to $1.20B. Operating cash flow was $899M in the quarter — the underlying business still generates cash.

follow100Note: Kept as profit is negative: after a $12.08 tax bill per $100 of revenue, Viatris lost $8.67 for every $100 it took in.
